title: Sierra Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Emily Stone (Sierra Head of Search), Dev Patel (ML Eng), Riley Brooks (CTO)
summary: Discovery call to understand Sierra Analytics' use of embeddings for search and reranking. Primary goals: integrate Redwood hosted/dedicated for embeddings + rerank, vector DB selection and architecture (hybrid search with lexical + vector), throughput and latency targets, security requirements (VPC, SOC2, KMS), success criteria for a 6-week POC. Next steps: send pricing and security pack, set up technical deep-dive and benchmarking plan, customer to share sample dataset and query profile.
topics: vector DB options and integration patterns
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
action_items: Ava Chen: Send pricing sheet and onboarding checklist by 2026-03-06
Marco Ruiz: Draft benchmarking plan and provide sample scripts by 2026-03-08
Dev Patel: Share 10k sample documents + query logs (anonymized) by 2026-03-06
Emily Stone: Confirm latency SLO and throughput targets by 2026-03-05
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security docs
Customer to share sample dataset and query distribution
Agree on POC success criteria and timeline (6 weeks suggested)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, really excited to chat through embeddings and rerank, quick intro — I’m Ava, AE for this region, Marco from our SE team will cover tech details
[00:10] Emily (Sierra): Hi, Emily here, Head of Search at Sierra, happy to dive in — we have Dev and Riley on as well
[00:16] Dev (Sierra): Hey all, Dev, ML Eng, mainly responsible for infra and model infra
[00:22] Marco (Redwood): Great, quick agenda: understand current stack, what you want from rerank, throughput/latency, security, and POC scoping
[00:30] Riley (Sierra): Sounds good, we can run through our current pain points first
[00:35] Emily: Right now we have a hybrid search setup — OpenSearch for indexing and BM25 for recall, then we do a TensorFlow-based rerank with a bi-encoder embedding model. It kind of works but costs are spiking and latency for rerank at 99th is unpredictable
[00:52] Dev: We store vectors in a managed vector db (we've tried Pinecone and an in-house FAISS service) — dimensionality is 768, about 10M vectors, mostly short docs and product descriptions
[01:05] Marco: OK so 10M vectors at 768 dims — what throughput are you trying to hit for rerank? QPS or per query vector lookups?
[01:12] Emily: Typical peak QPS is about 120 qps for queries, each query we want top 200 candidates from vector recall and then rerank the top 20 with cross-encoder (expensive)
[01:24] Ava: And what are your latency targets end-to-end?
[01:27] Emily: Ideally p95 under 250ms for the whole search+rerank pipeline; p99 under 400ms would be OK, but we care a lot about consistency
[01:37] Marco: Clear. Two levers: move heavier reranking to a lighter cross-encoder or use rerank as a second stage with cached KV for popular prefixes. Also deployment mode matters — hosted vs dedicated affects tail latencies and cold starts
[01:50] Dev: We were looking at Redwood because we like the idea of predictable throughput with Dedicated, but we'd also like to understand Hosted — cost differences, and private for data residency if needed
[02:00] Riley: Also security — SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS integration are must-haves for us
[02:08] Marco: Got it. Quick note on embeddings: you mentioned 768 dims — are you fixed on that or can you tradeoff dims for latency/cost?
[02:15] Emily: Our current model is 768 but we're open to smaller dims if quality holds. We use a combination of semantic recall and lexical features, hybrid search is core to relevancy
[02:25] Marco: Good. For 10M vectors at 768, latency to get top-200 neighbors depends on index type (HNSW, IVF, PQ). With Redwood Dedicated we can co-locate the vector store and embedding generation to avoid network hops. For hosted, we often pipeline to managed vector DBs like Pinecone, but that adds network tail and egress costs
[02:45] Dev: Is the vector store something Redwood manages or do we bring our own? We want to know integration patterns
[02:51] Marco: Redwood can host embeddings service and we support connectors to vector DBs — two common patterns: 1) Redwood-hosted embeddings + push vectors to your chosen vector DB (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate); 2) Dedicated/Private where we manage the inference on your infra and you keep vectors in your VPC — both are supported
[03:08] Emily: Hybrid search: right now we do BM25 recall + vector rerank. Any recommendations on recall size? We pull 1k results from BM25 then embed and rerank — it's expensive
[03:18] Marco: Pulling 1k is large — typical patterns are 200-400 for BM25 then vector rerank to top 50-100 before cross-encoder. Also consider doing a cheap semantic filter using low-dim or sparse embeddings to prune early
[03:32] Dev: For throughput, our cross-encoder is the bottleneck. If we rerank 50 items per query at 120 qps that's heavy. Can Redwood run efficient batching for rerank?
[03:44] Marco: Yes, continuous batching and request coalescing are part of our runtime. We can batch cross-encoder calls and serve with quantized models to reduce GPU memory footprint. The tradeoff is latency vs batch size — for p95 under 250ms you want small batches with high-priority lanes or a Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs
[04:02] Riley: How about model size — cross-encoder we're using a 6B model, could we use a smaller distilled model?
[04:09] Marco: Distillation is a common approach — using a 220M-600M cross-encoder for rerank can retain much of the quality with much lower latency. We can recommend quantization profiles and kernel choices for the model architecture to hit your SLOs
[04:23] Emily: Any guidance on dimensionality vs recall quality? If we go from 768 to 384 or 256, what do we lose?
[04:30] Marco: It depends on the model and training; often 384 with good training gives near-parity on many product search datasets. We recommend an A/B where you generate embeddings at both dims and test offline quality metrics (recall@k, MRR) before committing
[04:46] Dev: For the POC, we want to test: 1) end-to-end latency at target QPS, 2) quality parity vs current reranker, 3) operational cost. Is that in line with Redwood's standard POC scope?
[04:58] Ava: Yes absolutely. Typical POC: 4-6 weeks, Redwood provides support to run benchmarks, SE-led tuning, and a canary deployment if Dedicated is chosen. We'll include benchmarking scripts and we can run a hosted pilot first if you want to move faster
[05:12] Emily: Security checklist — can Redwood support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, and audit logs?
[05:20] Marco: Yes. Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem options; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS integrations and audit logging. We are SOC2 compliant and can share the security pack — though exact options depend on contract level
[05:32] Riley: What about data residency — we need EU-only for some clients
[05:36] Ava: We can pin region and host inference in EU regions for Dedicated or Private. Hosted can also be region-separated but has some constraints; we'll highlight that in the security docs
[05:46] Dev: Latency — can you give rough numbers for topologies? Like hosted-to-Pinecone vs dedicated co-located?
[05:53] Marco: Roughly: hosted + external vector DB can add 30-80ms network tail; dedicated co-located can bring that sub-10-30ms. Cross-encoder latency depends on model and batch size — smaller quantized models can be 10-40ms per example with right infra; larger ones higher
[06:10] Emily: Cost — is Dedicated significantly more expensive? We want predictable unit costs, not surprised by token billing
[06:16] Ava: Dedicated is capex-like commitment but gives predictability and lower per-token cost at scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but can be more variable. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to reduce unit cost as part of the POC
[06:31] Dev: Are there reference benchmarks we can see? Preferably for product search or e-comm type workloads
[06:36] Marco: We'll share a benchmark deck and a sample spreadsheet. Also, we can run a quick spike against your sample dataset for apples-to-apples numbers
[06:43] Riley: Who will own infra for the POC? We prefer Redwood to provision a sandbox Dedicated pool if possible, else a hosted pilot to prove concept
[06:52] Ava: We'll include options in the pricing: hosted pilot vs short-term dedicated sandbox. For legal, we can outline scope in an MSA addendum for the POC
[06:59] Emily: On vector DB choice — we're evaluating Pinecone vs Milvus. Any particular pros/cons when paired with Redwood?
[07:07] Marco: Both are fine. Pinecone is fully managed and easy to integrate; Milvus/Weaviate give more control (and can be self-hosted in your VPC). For latency predictability, self-hosted in the same VPC as Redwood Private is best. For hosted scenarios, Pinecone often has lower ops burden
[07:24] Dev: A couple housekeeping: query patterns — many short tail queries, some long-form queries, 25% of traffic is personalization; we'll share logs
[07:33] Marco: Perfect. For personalized signals we recommend storing user context as a small blackbox embedding and doing a hybrid scoring pipeline to avoid re-embedding large context per request
[07:42] Emily: Any risks you foresee?
[07:45] Marco: Main risks: 1) quality regressions when reducing dims or distilling — mitigate with eval sets; 2) cost surprises if batch sizes are misconfigured; 3) data egress if vectors live off-host — mitigate with co-location or private deploy
[07:58] Riley: OK can we summarize next steps?
[08:01] Ava: Sure — I'll send pricing + security pack; Marco will send benchmark plan and scripts; Dev will share sample dataset and query logs; we schedule SE deep-dive next week to scope POC details; we'll aim to decide on deployment mode by end of week after reviewing docs
[08:15] Emily: Thanks — that works for me
[08:17] Dev: Thanks, looking forward to the benchmark details
[08:20] Marco: Great, we'll follow up with links and a proposed calendar invite, plus a short checklist for the POC
[08:28] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email
[48:00] (call ends)
